name: Blaverism
summary: Blaverism is a Valencian regionalism that arose in the Transition against Joan Fuster's claim that Valencians and Catalans share one language and one nation. It holds that Valencian identity, history and language are distinct from Catalan and that Valencia belongs within the Spanish nation, and it fixed on symbols (the blue-fringed senyera, the name Kingdom of Valencia, its own spelling norms). Scholars call it conservative, populist, regionalist, Spanish-nationalist and essentialist. It is a reactive identity movement and its own texts say little outside language, identity and Spanish unity.
scope: Valencian identity defended as distinct from Catalan, from the Transition (late 1970s) onward, as stated by the institutions that carry it (Real Acadèmia de Cultura Valenciana, Lo Rat Penat, Unió Valenciana and the GAV as described by scholars) and as analysed by Flor, Climent-Ferrando and Arreaza-Aguilera. It excludes the positions of the right-wing parties on economics, ethics and foreign policy, and excludes Valencianists who accept the unity of Catalan (Fuster's current).

sources.title: Estatutos de la Real Academia de Cultura Valenciana
sources.author: Real Academia de Cultura Valenciana (RACV)
sources.usedFor: The Academy's stated object: culture of the old Kingdom of Valencia and defence of the values and identity marks of the Valencian people; Valencian and Castilian as its official languages

sources.title: Comunicat institucional de la Secció de Llengua i Lliteratura Valencianes de la RACV (31 March 2006)
sources.author: RACV, language section
sources.usedFor: Its position that Valencian is a distinct language, that no international Romance-studies agreement backs the unity of Valencian and Catalan, and its rejection of the AVL

sources.title: Comunicat dirigit al Comité d'Experts del Consell d'Europa (3 March 2020)
sources.author: Lo Rat Penat, RACV, Real Societat Valenciana d'Agricultura i Deports, Ateneu Mercantil de Valéncia
sources.usedFor: Joint blaverist-institution statement: Valencian is the only legitimate name and a language distinct from Catalan, within the Spanish Constitution and the 1982 Statute; Valencian and Castilian co-official

sources.title: Informe de la Secció de Llengua i Lliteratura Valencianes de la RACV sobre l'idioma valencià, sol·licitat pel Tribunal Suprem
sources.author: RACV, language section
sources.usedFor: The RACV's claim that Valencian is an independent language with continuous written history since the 13th century and before, and its reading of the co-official status of Valencian and Castilian

sources.title: Llengua Valenciana (Secció de Llengua i Lliteratura Valencianes, RACV)
sources.author: RACV, language section
sources.usedFor: The Academy's own account of Valencian, its norms (Normes d'El Puig) and its claim that modern Valencian is the natural evolution of the language of the medieval classics

sources.title: La instrumentalització mediàtica de la identitat valenciana: el discurs anticatalanista de Las Provincias (1978-1999)
sources.author: Vicent Flor Moreno, Arxius de Ciències Socials 23 (2010)
sources.usedFor: Sociological definition of blaverism: anti-Catalanism dressed as Valencianism, regional identity subordinated to Spanish nationalism, populism, the role of Las Provincias

sources.title: La Batalla de València... i el que vingué després
sources.author: Vicent Flor, Eines 40 (2021)
sources.usedFor: Blaverism's conservative continuity of regional identity, subordination of the Kingdom of Valencia to the Spanish nation, denial of the unity of Catalan and of any common cultural affiliation, and the symbolic settlement it obtained (name, flag, anthem)

sources.title: The origins and evolution of language secessionism in Valencia
sources.author: Vicent Climent-Ferrando, Mercator Working Papers 18 (2005)
sources.usedFor: What the blaverist camp claims (Valencian independent of Catalan, plot against Valencian identity, blue-fringed flag, name Kingdom of Valencia) and the identity and juridical lines of argument it settled on

sources.title: El blaverismo y la extrema derecha valenciana: un análisis de las relaciones y la evolución
sources.author: Idoia Arreaza-Aguilera, XV Congreso AECPA (2021)
sources.usedFor: Defining traits of blaverism after Flor (anti-Catalanism, conservatism, regionalism, Spanish nationalism, essentialism); institutional blaverism renounces violence while the street wing (GAV) used it

sources.title: Declaration on the name and distinct character of Valencian (22 August 2023)
sources.author: Real Acadèmia de Cultura Valenciana
sources.usedFor: Full seven-page declaration downloaded: separate linguistic identity, official versions and coofficial recognition.

sources.title: Fare la Spagna dalla periferia. L’anticatalanismo e la Regione Valenzana (2013)
sources.author: Vicent Flor
sources.usedFor: Full article downloaded and searched; identity, symbols, regional autonomy within Spain and RACV’s relation to the movement.

missingStatements.text: A region may give its local language variety its own official name and spelling standard, even where linguists class it as the same language as a neighbouring region's.
missingStatements.rationale: The RACV's Normes d'El Puig and its 2006 and 2020 statements demand that Valencian keep its own name and norms against the AVL's unitary standard and the Council of Europe's "Valencian/Catalan".

missingStatements.text: A region's flag and official name should differ visibly from those of the neighbouring region with which it shares a language.
missingStatements.rationale: Blaverists won the blue-fringed senyera and the name Comunitat Valenciana rather than País Valencià, and had proposed Kingdom of Valencia, to set Valencia apart from Catalonia.

notes:
Searched, theme by theme: language and identity (RACV statutes, communiqués, Supreme Court report, language site), Spanish unity and regional status (scholarship, RACV and joint statements), symbols and names (Flor, Climent-Ferrando), violence (Arreaza-Aguilera), and economy, government, society, world, liberty, ecology, technology, means and globalism (nothing the movement itself states). Unió Valenciana's 1995 programme (market economy with a subsidiary public sector, Valencian language and culture, regional financing) was read in Crespo Hellin's study but is a party's platform, not the movement's, so it answers nothing. Old answers deduced from the right-wing parties are null. A thin record is expected: the sources are silent outside language, identity and Spanish unity. Blaverist writers' own books (Broseta, Calpe) and Las Provincias editorials could not be opened; the movement's critics supply most of the scholarship.
